The PIPELINE_DIR sed substitution has no check that it actually matched -- if templates/pre-push's literal default-value line ever changes without updating this sed pattern, the installed hook silently keeps the wrong PIPELINE_DIR. chmod +x ... || true swallows any chmod failure silently; git ignores a non-executable hook with no warning, so a chmod failure on an unusual filesystem could ship a hook that never fires while install-hook.sh still reports success. Not reproduced (chmod succeeded normally here) -- reasoned finding, not empirically forced.

BASE resolution falls through to HEAD~1 if no origin/main, origin/master, main, or master resolves -- for a first multi-commit push this would silently narrow the reviewed diff to just the last commit. Not triggered in this repo's actual push (origin/master resolves correctly) -- unexercised fallback path, not a live bug.

grep -rqs "$SHA" "$REPORTS" is a substring match anywhere in any report file, not anchored to a structured 'Reviewed:' field -- SHA is always the full 40-hex-char form (confirmed at line 77), so accidental collision is cryptographically negligible; the real looseness is that a report merely mentioning the sha in passing (not as an actual review) would satisfy the check. Self-authored reports, not adversary-controlled, so low practical risk -- named as a known limitation.

self-review found and fixed one issue before send-off: _MATRIX_SKIP_LOCK initially read from environment like the public MATRIX_ROUTER/MATRIX_LOCK overrides, but as an internal-only var (sibling _MATRIX_TABLE/_MATRIX_LOAD_FAILED are plain resets, never env-sourced) this would let anyone controlling the caller's environment silently disable the lock check. Fixed: plain reset, set only by --freeze's own code path. Re-verified 35/35 matrix tests after the fix

HARD GATE. Threat model considered: (1) env-var bypass of the new check -- found live during self-review (_MATRIX_SKIP_LOCK was env-settable), fixed before send-off, see G6 note. (2) hash injection/format-string in the lock file write or read paths -- printf uses %s placeholders throughout, awk read is a plain first-field extraction, no eval/interpolation into an execution context. (3) collision/preimage on the sha256 comparison -- standard cryptographic assumption, same trust level as any lockfile scheme (npm/pip), not a practical concern for this threat model. (4) the explicitly out-of-scope case -- a single commit editing core/01-router.md and tools/lib/matrix.lock together with intent defeats this check; documented as a non-goal in the spec, same review-dependency every other file in this repo already has. No other input surface: MATRIX_ROUTER/MATRIX_LOCK path overrides are pre-existing attack surface (env-controllable since matrix.sh's original version), not new to this change
